name: Traffic light LED module (red, yellow, green)
description: Three LEDs (red, yellow, green) arranged like a traffic light on one small board, each with its own on-board current-limiting resistor (marked 221/471, i.e. 220 Ω / 470 Ω) and a shared ground (common cathode). Drive R, Y or G high from a GPIO to light that LED; no supply pin and no driver chip. Works from 3.3–5 V logic. Sold as: Keyestudio KS0310 Traffic Light Module (black PCB, 4-pin header R, Y, G, GND), and the many look-alike traffic light LED modules with the same R/Y/G/GND header.
eli5: A tiny traffic light: switch a pin on and the red, yellow or green light comes on, so you can make your own crossing signal.

pins.name: R
pins.description: Red LED anode through its on-board resistor: high = red on, low = off. A few mA from a 3.3 V GPIO.

pins.name: Y
pins.description: Yellow LED anode through its on-board resistor: high = yellow on, low = off.

pins.name: G
pins.description: Green LED anode through its on-board resistor: high = green on, low = off.

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Common cathode of all three LEDs; connect to the microcontroller's GND.

supplierQuery: traffic light LED module R Y G GND red yellow green
buildNotes: There is no VCC pin: each LED is powered by the GPIO wired to R, Y or G, through the resistor already on the board. Only GND goes to the board's ground.
Logic level 3.3–5 V (Keyestudio rating). From a 3.3 V ESP32 or Pico the LEDs are a little dimmer than from 5 V, but each draws only a few mA, well within a GPIO's limit.
Do not add a resistor and do not wire R/Y/G to 5V or 3V3 directly unless you want that LED permanently on; never apply more than 5 V.
Create the pins with value=0 so all lights start off, then switch them in the sequence green -> yellow -> red.

example.code:
from machine import Pin
import time

# Each LED has its own resistor on the module: GPIO high = LED on.
red = Pin({R}, Pin.OUT, value=0)
yellow = Pin({Y}, Pin.OUT, value=0)
green = Pin({G}, Pin.OUT, value=0)

def show(r, y, g, name):
    red.value(r)
    yellow.value(y)
    green.value(g)
    print(name)

while True:
    show(0, 0, 1, 'GREEN')
    time.sleep(2)
    show(0, 1, 0, 'YELLOW')
    time.sleep(1)
    show(1, 0, 0, 'RED')
    time.sleep(2)

test.title: Green, yellow and red light up in turn
